(2) NEW b_alu14_c83: a low-nibble-0xf 14-byte integer/simd ALU (byte+2==0x83) at high-nibbles 0x3f/0x5f/0x7f, byte+1=(reg<<1)|1, byte+3=byte+1-1 register pair; back-to-back spacing = exactly 14. (3) if_push GENERALIZED: 0x0f byte+1 low-nibble 5 (predicate/condition high-nibble) is the 4-byte execution-mask PUSH, ~100 corpus leaders, each followed by a 0f 01 jump_cond. (4) marshalling: `20 {01,81,82} | 0f..` 2-byte predicate-mask operand words, and a 2-byte b_alu14 PREP word (byte0=(dst<<4)|2, byte+1=(dst<<1)|1) preceding a b_alu14.

descriptors.semantics: RAY-TRACING ray-data / traversal-stack memory op (14B). byte0 0x5f (low-nibble 0xf, the memory-family low nibble, sibling of the 0xdf AS-load and the 0x67/0xe7 buffer load/store), byte+1 == 0x02 (addressing sub-op). The store/spill-side companion of the 0xdf AS-data load: fetches/spills the ray struct + per-node BVH traversal-stack state during the (software) traversal loop, and carries the ray_data PAYLOAD copy-in/out for custom intersection functions (count scales with payload size). byte+2 = mode (0x54/0x56 = the original memory markers; 0x04/0x64 = further address-space/cache variants, byte-identical bodies). The byte+1==0x10 (12B load-index) and byte+1==0x11 (6B short) forms are SEPARATE descriptors (rt_ray_mem_ldidx / rt_ray_mem_short); the old blunt `byte+2 in {0x54,0x56} -> 14` mislengthed those.
descriptors.provenance: inferred (byte-diff, EXP-O2C + EXP-M4-13 R4): byte0 0x5f present in every raytracing:: kernel (12-28 per kernel) and ABSENT from a hand-written software triangle loop (EXP-0023 control). R4: 1017/1657 byte+1==0x02,byte+2==0x54 forms sit back-to-back at exactly 14 in the corpus; the 0x04 form (233 own-corpus leaders) is byte-identical to the 0x54 form modulo byte+2. Field bit-packing not splice-validated (no GPU dispatch).

descriptors.semantics: RAY-TRACING ray-data memory op, load-INDEX variant (12B). byte0 0x5f, byte+1 == 0x10, byte+2 == 0x54. Mirrors the 0x67 device-load space+index addressing byte (byte+1 low nibble 0 = indexed). 12 bytes (NOT 14): all 32 corpus occurrences sit back-to-back at gap 12 (`5f 10 54 00 00 01 26 c0 60 4f c8 00` then the next 0x5f). The old blunt byte+2-only rule wrongly gave it 14.
descriptors.provenance: byte-diff EXP-M4-13 R4 (own-MSL): back-to-back spacing = 12 across 32 occurrences (rq_pred / RT-query kernels). Length bracketed by the next 0x5f leader; body raw. Not splice-validated.

descriptors.semantics: RAY-TRACING ray-data memory op, SHORT form (6B). byte0 0x5f, byte+1 == 0x11 (the 0x67 load index+1 addressing byte), byte+2 == 0x54, body `<b3> 00 00`. 6 bytes: ALL 92 corpus occurrences sit back-to-back at gap 6 (`5f 11 54 04 00 00` immediately followed by the next 0x5f ray-data op). The old blunt byte+2-only rule wrongly gave it 14.
descriptors.provenance: byte-diff EXP-M4-13 R4 (own-MSL): back-to-back spacing = 6 across 92 occurrences (rq_pred / RT-query kernels). Length bracketed by the immediately-following 0x5f leader. Not splice-validated.

descriptors.semantics: low-nibble-0xf 14-byte integer/simd ALU (byte+2 == 0x83 form). A distinct opcode from the iadd2/imad 0x9f/0x1f family (byte+2 == 0x54): byte0 high nibble is a variant selector (0x3f/0x5f/0x7f observed), byte+1 = (reg<<1)|1 and byte+3 = byte+1-1 form a register operand pair, and the tail carries a fixed `03 00 80 <ZZ> 00 00 03 00` frame plus a trailing register word. Appears back-to-back in the RT-traversal coordinate / index getters and the log2(N) shuffle+multiply integer simd-prefix/product reduction trees. Exact arithmetic (which lane/register combine) NOT resolved -- structural/length only.
descriptors.provenance: byte-diff EXP-M4-13 R4 (own-MSL): back-to-back spacing = exactly 14 across the corpus (e.g. `3f 07 83 06 03 00 80 04 00 00 03 00 12 01` then the next `3f`/`7f` op); byte+1/byte+3 register-pair relation (b3=b1-1) holds across all high-nibble variants. Not splice-validated (M4 compile-only, no GPU dispatch).

descriptors.semantics: execution-mask PUSH / if-enter, PREDICATE variant (4B). byte0 0x0f, byte+1 low nibble == 5 with a non-zero HIGH nibble selecting a predicate / condition register (the plain 0x05 base is if_push). byte+2 = CF marker (0x54 outer / 0x56 last-use), byte+3 = nesting level. Pairs with the following 0f 01 jump_cond as the if/loop test-and-branch in the RT-query and integer simd-prefix kernels; paired with a later 0f 06 pop_reconverge.
descriptors.provenance: byte-diff EXP-M4-13 R4 (own-MSL): ~100 corpus leaders (`0f 15 54 21`, `0f 45 54 21`, `0f 25 56 02`, ...) each bracketed to 4 bytes by the immediately-following `0f 01 54 <off>` jump_cond. Generalizes the RT-ISA-FIX HW-validated b1==0x05 -> 4 push. Not splice-validated.

descriptors.semantics: 2-byte compact PREP word preceding a b_alu14 (byte+2==0x83 int/simd ALU). byte0 low nibble 2, high nibble = dst reg; byte+1 = (dst<<1)|1 (the compact register field, size bit set). A per-operand register declaration / high-half select emitted right before the 14-byte ALU op in the RT getter and integer simd-reduction trees. Distinct from the 6-byte low-nibble-2 min/max (whose byte+2 is a min/max op-select, not a b_alu14 leader).
descriptors.provenance: byte-diff EXP-M4-13 R4 (own-MSL): `72 0f | 3f 13 83 ..`, `52 0b | 3f 13 83 ..`, `82 11 | 3f 45 83 ..`, `92 13 | 3f 17 83 ..` -- prev op decodes cleanly (falu2) so the 2-byte word is a genuine leader, and byte0=(dst<<4)|2 / byte+1=(dst<<1)|1 holds across dst regs. Not splice-validated.

notes: byte0 low-nibble 0xf is a grab-bag of >=4-byte 'special' ops keyed on the HIGH nibble: control-flow (0x0f), integer add/sub imad (0x1f/0x9f, byte+2==0x54), the NEW byte+2==0x83 14-byte int/simd ALU (0x3f/0x5f/0x7f), the ray-data memory op (0x5f byte+1==0x02), function return (0x8f), matrix MAC (0xcf), AS-load (0xdf). b_alu14_c83 and iadd2 are DIFFERENT opcodes distinguished by byte+2 (0x83 vs 0x54).

rt_ray_mem byte+1 is the addressing sub-op (0x02 general 14B, 0x10 load-index 12B, 0x11 short 6B); byte+2 is an address-space/cache MODE (0x54/0x56 original markers + 0x04/0x64 variants with byte-identical bodies). The 0x04 form is the 'continuation' the task flagged: byte+2 is NOT a 0x54/0x56 memory-marker, which is why the old rule desynced on it.
if_push_pred (byte+1 low-nibble 5, high-nibble != 0) wins over the base if_push (byte+1==0x05 exactly, 16-bit match) by match specificity; fldexp (length 6) never collides (different length).

b_alu14_prep2 length is gated on the NEXT op being a b_alu14 (methodologically weak but zero-false-positive: real low-nibble-2 min/max carries a min/max op-select in byte+2, never 0x3f/5f/7f-with-byte+4==0x83). The SFU-prep variant (`82 4a 7f 80 86`, byte+1 != (dst<<1)|1) is left UNRESOLVED.
